text:
yara: thinking about a small 'unit-econ' mini card for the Console list view showing per-model USD/token and amortized cache savings. Question: should default be USD/token or % savings? Also need to know what telemetry fields we must add.

tom: USD/token is what finance loves, but percent is easier to scan. Maybe show percent big + small USD/token under it.

anna: Agree. Percent prominent, USD/token secondary. Also add a tiny sparkline for last 7d and a tooltip that expands to token counts + sample confidence.

ben: Telemetry note: we need tokenized_input_count and tokenized_output_count in ingress to compute per-invocation tokens. Also include tokenization_version (model-specific) because different model variants tokenize differently.

sara: If we add token counts to hot events that's high cardinality. Suggest sampled enrichment: default 0.5% for list-level cards, 5% for detailed route view. Attach sample_weight to each enriched event to reconstruct totals.

yara: Good call. UX: when sample_rate < 1% show a little badge "sampled" with hover text: "Numbers estimated from sampled lineage. Click for explain."

tom: API shape proposal: /econ/preview?window_days=7&sample_rate=0.005&route=... returns flat rows: route, model_variant, pct_savings, usd_per_token_est, tokens_saved_est, sample_rate_applied, tokenization_version. Example payload (conceptual):```json
{"route":"checkout","model_variant":"rwd-13b-q4_0","pct_savings":8.2,"usd_per_token_est":0.000012,"tokens_saved_est":3421,"sample_rate":0.005,"tokenization_version":"v2"}
```

anna: UX nit: show pct_savings with +/- CI as an opacity band on the sparkline. Replace raw CI numbers with a confidence pill (high/med/low) and allow expansion to exact CI. Also add an "Explain" modal that shows tokenized example invocations and how savings were attributed.

ben: Analytics will need a reconciliation job to compare the sample-weighted estimate to the billing invoice per model SKU daily. If discrepancy > 8% for 3 consecutive days, auto-increase sample_rate for affected routes.

sara: Ops: enriched events must be async. We'll enqueue on the fast path and drop to a best-effort stream to keep latency unaffected. For hotspot routes we can enable a short buffer and background flush.

yara: What about multi-model chains? If a single route fans out to multiple model calls, we need per-call attribution. We should emit call_index and parent_call_id in enriched lineage.

ben: Good point. We'll reconstruct chain-level USD by aggregating sample_weighted per-call tokens and applying model variant cost rates. Need to remember to store model_price_per_token history for accurate backfills.

anna: Rollout UX: allow "Preview cost impact" from rollout panel for canary only. We call /econ/preview with the canary routing policy param and show delta vs baseline (percent + USD). Add a warning when sample_rate < 1% that numbers are approximate.

sara: Backfill option for enterprise customers: we can run a higher-sample job on historical logs for 30d to generate more accurate unit-econ for billing reconciliation. Ops will gate on customer consent.

yara: Last question: where do we show tokenization_version? Important for debugging token delta between variants.

tom: Show it in the explain modal and surface a small tag on the detailed model row. No need in the list card.

ops-bot: Canary helper: scheduled job econ/reconcile -> staging at 2024-10-05T02:00:00Z. Use flag feature/econ-preview.

yara: OK I'll file three PRs: 1) telemetry schema changes (token counts, tokenization_version, call_index) 2) /econ/preview API + sample_weight support 3) Console mini-card + explain modal + rollout preview wiring. @anna will own copy and mockups.

anna: on it. I'll post Figma link when draft is ready.

ben: I'll start the reconciliation job skeleton and sample-weight aggregator.

sara: I'll implement async enrichment pipeline and hot-route buffering.

yara: Thanks all. We'll iterate sample_rate defaults after the first reconciliation run.
